note: Public, redistributable FM-1 packages. Newest first; every package is SHA-256 and FM-1 identity checked.

firmwares.name: Smileyface
firmwares.author: pbarilla
firmwares.about: You're making acid, baby! Smash that LFO button until you hear something you like, and then twist those knobs! Now with 100% more FX! A truly trippy experience! Built on Chipbox.

firmwares.name: AISLING
firmwares.author: CU_STE
firmwares.about: A generative Irish ambient instrument: harps in a jig's threes and a flute over a drone, with surf, wind and rain. Eight pieces play themselves for ever; play along on its keys, a keyboard or a DAW. Its visualiser paints it as an Irish landscape, and its site shows how to build that into a touch…

firmwares.name: Chipbox
firmwares.author: pbarilla
firmwares.about: A ultra-refined Chiptune music editor, featuring over 35 classic chips such as NES, Gameboy, heck even the Sunsoft 5B! Gimmick fans rejoice!

firmwares.name: KARMA
firmwares.author: Ariel Muchnik
firmwares.about: A four-track groovebox: an acid bass or a Juno-style poly, physical modelling, two dozen synthesis models and a drum synth. A 64-step sequencer with song mode, generators that write parts on one chord plan, pixel characters, and USB audio with six stems, MIDI out and DAW sync.

firmwares.name: Quartet
firmwares.author: MammothCheese
firmwares.about: A four-track groovebox that plays like a four-piece band: lead, pads, bass and drums. 40 sounds and 10 drum kits, 5 effect pedals, an arpeggiator, step and live recording, and a song sequencer where each instrument follows its own arrangement.

firmwares.name: Guru-600
firmwares.author: Marc Massé
firmwares.about: The FM-1 becomes a Prophet-600: 255 sounds (the 100 factory programs, 100 from the free 2022 collection, 55 of its own), a web editor in 7 languages with a panel inspired by the Prophet-600, four tracks with sequencer, arpeggiator, morph and two insert effects each. Based on Felucca.

firmwares.name: Ravel
firmwares.author: De-Pattern
firmwares.about: An eight-track groovebox for sound design: thirteen synth engines, struck percussion and 33 drum machines after the Machinedrum, on an influence grid where any track can trigger, excite or modulate any other.

firmwares.name: B3 ORGAN
firmwares.author: R-Jeb
firmwares.about: A B3 tonewheel organ: 91 wheels, nine drawbars, key click, vibrato and chorus, percussion, overdrive, reverb and a Leslie, computed from setBfree's own data and measured against it. All 110 setBfree programs and its default MIDI controllers.

firmwares.name: Pocket Band
firmwares.author: elpabl0
firmwares.about: A band in your FM-1. Pick a spot on a map of 16 genre towns and it writes a four-piece sketch: drums, bass, keys and lead in one key. Re-roll parts, audition players, jam, morph, play punch-in effects, edit steps, save four slots. With a rhythm game played over your own drum part.

firmwares.name: FM-FAM
firmwares.author: David Amo
firmwares.about: Dfam style 16-step sequencer and a drum synth: two oscillators with 16 wave types, a kick with its own sequencer, parameter locks, a sound saved per pattern, an effects chain, random pages, scales, presets and projects.

firmwares.name: ChoralRoot
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.about: A Telepathic Orchid-style chord instrument: one hand plays roots, the other shapes chords; voicings, performance modes, bass and a looper.

firmwares.name: bocjuhn
firmwares.author: ryuji kanagawa
firmwares.about: Six tracks, eight engines. RC10: RYUJI hybrid VA + samples focused on 808/909, clean playback, longer metallic tails, editable kits and random locks. Integer DSP, unchanged RAM allocation. Physical hardware validation pending.

firmwares.name: Elixir
firmwares.author: Dan Majka
firmwares.about: A super powerful drum synth and sequencer that started as a port of the Erica Synths LXR-02 and kept going. Make a beat in two minutes, then dig into 29 sound engines, deep effects, generative sequencing, live performance tricks, MIDI control and 8-channel USB audio.

firmwares.name: RAMBEAVER
firmwares.author: Trust This Mechanism
firmwares.about: A side-scrolling action game with synthesized music, sound effects and character voices. Defend the dam, ride through robot city, fly to the data center and stop Mother.

firmwares.name: Trumpagotchi
firmwares.author: Trust This Mechanism
firmwares.about: An unofficial parody virtual pet with a playable pentatonic keyboard. Feed, praise, clean up after and rest the pet. When he's happy, he joins your playing on bongos.

firmwares.name: Kris Jangle
firmwares.author: w33tSnx
firmwares.about: Kris Jangle is a Christmas game for the FM-1: it plays the start of a carol and you replay it on the keys, building three notes per level up to the whole song. Four carols, three play modes from guided EASY to sound-only HARD, and Grump Mode on three misses.

firmwares.name: ASS-ID
firmwares.author: altessproduction
firmwares.about: The ATEK303 acid groovebox plus a drum track on the same clock: eight synthesized TR-808/909/707 voices, no samples, a seeded 64-step generator with mutations and LOCK for both tracks, an 8x16 drum matrix, swing, three kits, drive, chorus, delay, reverb and eight factory presets.

firmwares.name: Felucca 8 Patterns
firmwares.author: echoe
firmwares.about: Felucca 1.5.1 with eight sequences a track to switch between and chain one after another; the user samples are left out to make room.

firmwares.name: SATIE-1
firmwares.author: OCKM Studio
firmwares.about: Erik. Evolved. Ten Satie pieces become an evolving electronic soundtrack in five moods. Choose a tune, set the pace and blend Solo, Duet or Trio. Shape each instrument, add vinyl colour and synced delay, or simply let it play. GLO opens the quick guide.

firmwares.name: PLAYA
firmwares.author: JFS
firmwares.about: A performance firmware built on Optimist: two synth layers on one keyboard (layer, split, blend or single), drums with a simple step sequencer, send effects, Bluetooth MIDI keyboards, and one easy to read screen with knobs 1-4 to edit all parameters. 5 engines, 32 drum kits, 135 presets.

firmwares.name: JIANT FM
firmwares.author: juanjiant-bit
firmwares.about: A bio-synthetic groovebox: six tracks drawn as living beings in thermal colours, eight engines (FM6 with Dexed, analog, phase, voice…), mutating macros, song mode from SLOOP. Not yet tested much on a real FM-1.

firmwares.name: M-PYRE
firmwares.author: History Of Sky
firmwares.about: A riffbox for rock and metal: real guitar, bass and drum samples, an amp engine with cabinet IRs, pedals and guitar effects, plus all of SLOOP's synth engines. Bend strings, play whammy, wah and palm mutes live, record on the 4-track and turn riffs into songs.

firmwares.name: DUELL
firmwares.author: OSCILL/R
firmwares.about: A MULTIMORPHING bitimbral synth: two complete parts, three ways to play them together, and a morph that glides between two versions of every sound. Ten engines including wavetables, twin filters, effects and a mod matrix. Layer, dual or stereo mode. Velocity sensitivity and aftertouch. Dual core.

firmwares.name: hawk-chua
firmwares.author: plieuwski
firmwares.about: Noise and modeling synth with GM-style presets (4 banks, 512) and a 4-track tape recorder: each voice a live Chua circuit or noise program, through vactrol gates into resonators and piano, drum, voice, flute, brass, bowed, reed and bird waveguides, with temple, cathedral and mosque reverbs. GM…

firmwares.name: Veffbox
firmwares.author: Veff
firmwares.about: Resampling sound design. Build one sound from FM, analog or 808-style drums, play it as notes, steps or strummed chords, add 6 LFOs, 3 envelopes and 8 FX, then resample it into a new source. Every resample keeps its recipe, so a 64-sound bank of generation trees rebuilds bit for bit.

firmwares.name: Kitten Rack
firmwares.author: Black Kitten Devices
firmwares.about: A Eurorack-style modular synth: 56 modules (VCOs, a Moog-style ladder, a Moog 960-style sequencer that plays your voices, a low pass gate, Turing, Marbles, chaos, effects) patched with cables on the FM-1 itself, a 64-step sequencer with live recording, 33 factory patches, visuals, USB audio and…

firmwares.name: Frodhes
firmwares.author: Leonardo Mirabal
firmwares.about: An electric piano, vibraphone and marimba, physically modelled, no samples, with drive, tremolo or wah, phaser, chorus, delay and reverb (hall, plate, infinite), tap tempo and MIDI clock sync, an arpeggiator, a sequencer, scales and presets.

firmwares.name: CoralFlower
firmwares.author: FicusFicusov
firmwares.about: Chords after the Orchid, with controls made for the FM-1: one key plays a chord with a bass note. Also 27 scales, an arpeggiator, a sequencer with drums and a song mode, and a pixel flower that grows as you play.

firmwares.name: fm1-amy
firmwares.author: Dan Ellis
firmwares.about: A six-voice analog-style synth: AMY's emulations of the 128 Juno-60 factory patches, shaped with the AMYboard editor's patch knobs (oscillators, LFO, filter, envelopes, EQ, chorus, reverb, distortion) on eleven colour-coded pages. Plays over USB MIDI, and the AMYboard editor can edit it live.

firmwares.name: Miku-FM
firmwares.author: Michael Perry
firmwares.about: A singing songwriter: a pixel singer sings your songs in Japanese, consonants and all, over FM chords, bass and drums. Shape her voice with effects, harmony and five characters, write patterns or let her generate a whole song, and watch her dance. 8 song slots.

firmwares.name: keySTEP ONE
firmwares.author: dzwerg
firmwares.about: A four-track MIDI arranger and controller for the M-VAVE FM-1. Create patterns, songs and albums, switch patterns live, route USB and Bluetooth MIDI, and play sounds with the onboard General MIDI synth.

firmwares.name: Drumlab
firmwares.author: pbarilla
firmwares.about: Microtonic, for the FM-1! Roll the dice for a kit, build one from scratch, or bring in your Microtonic presets and patterns. Share kits and patterns as files, and send it all to your Teenage Engineering PO-32! Built on Chipbox!

firmwares.name: Bytemania
firmwares.author: lloyd (llozd)
firmwares.about: A bytebeat synth: play one-line formulas, tweak them with the knobs, and write your own, with a random button in the formula creator that is really fun. A beta, built on Dinghy.

firmwares.name: Caravel
firmwares.author: BonszaiMusic
firmwares.about: Multi-engine synth firmware with DRONE, STASIS texture capture, Pair Morph, and per-track Random Morph and Morph Journey for evolving, ambient and experimental sound design. Sequencer, MIDI Learn, USB audio.

firmwares.name: Tonitor
firmwares.author: Nuno Zimas
firmwares.about: Six tracks for live ambient and experimental music: three synth engines, patches generated by algorithm, free-length loops with up to ten overdubs each, a granulator, filters and a lush reverb.

firmwares.name: Matryoshka
firmwares.author: michael glaviano
firmwares.about: A modular synth for the FM-1: 30 factory patches built from nested modules, from classic polysynths to drum machines, each played with four knobs per page, plus a step sequencer with patterns and songs. Build your own patches in the browser editor and send them to the FM-1 over USB.

firmwares.name: sloop-DUB
firmwares.author: altessproduction
firmwares.about: The SLOOP groovebox for the M-VAVE FM-1, forked for dub: a three-band isolator with mute bands, a bipolar DJ filter, per-track echo throws, a tape echo with free time or synced divisions, an independent siren voice, skank, accents and slides — over the base SLOOP engines, kits and FM6.

firmwares.name: XENOLITH
firmwares.author: Unit_v743
firmwares.about: An experimental mono-track FM cell synthesizer with programmable oscillator routing, modulation, sequencing, a vintage circuit-derived filter, VCA, wavefolding, digital fidelity reduction and reverb. A load engine models physical voltage sag and progressively shrinks resource usage under stress.

firmwares.name: FOMAJAM
firmwares.author: konsumer
firmwares.about: A drum machine in the classic step-grid style: voices after the 909, 808, 707, 606, DMX and more, a machine per voice, accents and patterns. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: Hungry Travis
firmwares.author: Trust This Mechanism
firmwares.about: A spoon-feeding balance game with a beatless ambient soundtrack and voiced reactions. Balance a bean, guide the spoon and try to feed Travis. Every fifth bite sets off a transformation.

firmwares.name: DARK-1
firmwares.author: Polystellarflow
firmwares.about: Dark-music firmware for the FM-1: 21 genres, 210 pieces, from dark techno to dark ambient and darkwave. Wander evolves it on its own. Arp with Hold, Dice, step editor. New visuals, simpler settings, bigger text, plain-language help, SEL shortcut menu. 1.0.6: Advanced mode nowshows every page.

firmwares.name: Arctic Scream
firmwares.author: PolarPatch
firmwares.about: Long dark screaming ambient from the frozen Arctic. A living feedback loop creeps out of the cold and grows into a howl. Drones drift over the tundra as wind and every sound keeps moving after you let go. Four tracks, eight sound sources, endless reverb, shimmer and runaway echoes.

firmwares.name: Mutable Dreams
firmwares.author: Kid Bunka
firmwares.about: Six assignable synth tracks, or a Lo-Fi kit plus three synths. Explore 168 musical Biomes, 364 sounds and thirteen scales; receive BLE MIDI notes, CC and clock, shape chord journeys and generative rhythms, and play or edit in your browser.

firmwares.name: CORD
firmwares.author: Chase DeAnda
firmwares.about: Pick a chord progression, press Play, and play along with drums, bass and chords. Adjust the progression, sounds and groove to build backing tracks for practicing, jamming and writing songs.

firmwares.name: Penumbra
firmwares.author: Lunar Eclipse Forge
firmwares.about: A cinematic space drone you travel through, not one that plays itself. Five drone voices hold a pedal; turn PRESET and they glide to the next scene one voice at a time, or MORPH there by hand. Play VOX over it in key, loop it and the loop follows the key, or hold a key to bend and throw the sound.

firmwares.name: Sill
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: Generative 90s eurodance, pickled in 1995. Press PLAY and Sill writes a song and plays it: offbeat basses, piano and supersaw stabs, a chorus hook with a choir and a key change for the last chorus. Ten styles; steer it with four knobs, break it down, push the key up and play the hook yourself.

firmwares.name: Tuna
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: Generative music for the FM-1: it composes as it plays, melody, bass, accompaniment and percussion shaped by music theory out of controlled randomness. Pick a composer or one of 86 genres across eight decades and it plays in that manner, endlessly and never twice the same.

firmwares.name: Skiff
firmwares.author: illuminus5
firmwares.about: Six tracks of synths and drums with a groovebox's workflow: fourteen engines, a 64-step sequencer with chords, ratchets, trig conditions and locks, songs, PERFORM with scenes, six themes and a browser editor; FM6 sounds built from scratch on the unit. Built on Felucca, with most of Felucca 1.6.1's work brought over (the second core, MIDI LEARN, INSERT); Felucca's sounds and projects load. Also runs on the SMK-37 Pro. Coming from 1.x: 2.0 saves in new formats – update on Skiff's own page (it backs up and converts), or back up in its editor first.

firmwares.name: FM1 Audio Router
firmwares.author: MAX RAVE
firmwares.about: USB audio interface and Bluetooth audio receiver with FX

firmwares.name: JAMTRACK
firmwares.author: PhilipsKnobs
firmwares.about: A backing band to play over: drums, bass, chords and a synth line follow your chords in any key and time signature, in time with a loop pedal. 160 factory jams in 16 genres, a new jam at a press, your own synth line on a piano roll, and a companion web app to edit and share jams.

firmwares.name: FiMba-1
firmwares.author: jadamsowers
firmwares.about: A physically modelled kalimba: tines laid out like the real one, thumb-roll chords, mbira patterns, a sound hole to cover, grains, tape and a plate reverb. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: FMini-1
firmwares.author: Ruppert
firmwares.about: A three-oscillator monosynth in the spirit of the classic Moogs: a 24 dB/octave ladder filter, two contours, 100 factory patches, an arpeggiator, a sequencer and MIDI. Built on Felucca.

firmwares.name: Bigorna
firmwares.author: Nuno Zimas
firmwares.about: Rhythmic noise, power noise, industrial and IDM after the Elektron Digitone II: six tracks, four machines (4-OP, DRUM, WAVY, HIVE), parameter locks on a 16-step sequencer, a looper, send effects and USB audio.

firmwares.name: MONO2K
firmwares.author: Iñigo Hernandez
firmwares.about: Six mono machines in the spirit of Elektron's Monomachine: FM, superwaves, wavetables, a SID, a voice and four drum synths, one per track. A 64-step sequencer with parameter locks, trig conditions and ratchets, a lofi bus, four demo parts and a web patch editor.

firmwares.name: BEETLE BLUE
firmwares.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
firmwares.about: BEETLE BLUE turns your M-VAVE FM1 into a six-lane drum tracker. Build beats with BEETLE and MONOLITH kits, design custom drums, arrange songs, and perform setlists with Live Mode and hands-on effects.

firmwares.name: BEETLE
firmwares.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
firmwares.about: BEETLE transforms the FM-1 into a powerful 6-channel music workstation. Create beats, design sounds with retro-inspired synth engines, sequence entire songs, and perform with live effects. A complete pocket-sized tracker, drum machine, and synthesizer. Built for creativity, born out of passion.

firmwares.name: RUPTURE
firmwares.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
firmwares.about: A monophonic bass synth on Cycle Exchange Synthesis: two sub-oscillators, a ladder filter, Channel EQ, eight effects from MOSFET drive to octave fuzz, a step sequencer up to 128 steps and an arpeggiator.

firmwares.name: RemoteFM1
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.about: A firmware for your firmwares when using the app or a high quality 24bit DX7 rompler with 16 user carts and MIDI Controller when using the FM-1 by itself. BLE and USB supported!

firmwares.name: K-WASUB
firmwares.author: Omnipotard (Guizmoh)
firmwares.about: Runs on the latest FM-1 chip. A bass synth for DnB, dubstep, dub and techno: deep subs, reese, growls and 808s. Two of nine engines play together, the keys change the wobble live, and one button plus a knob puts an LFO on any setting. With drums, a bass sequencer and live FX pads.

firmwares.name: FRASIL
firmwares.author: Styves Goupil
firmwares.about: An ambient drone instrument: tap a key to latch a drone, a note or a chord in your key. Three layers a voice into a big reverb with shimmer and freeze; GLINT's icy FM bells on top, by hand, arpeggio or sequence; BASS a deep line below, held or sequenced; three LFOs keep it all moving.

firmwares.name: KAWA
firmwares.author: Omnipotard
firmwares.about: A pocket tracker for chiptune and IDM: six tracks of pulse, 4-bit wave, noise, 6-operator FM, drum kits and samples. Chain patterns into songs, chop breaks, and play 64 live effects (with K-GLITCH's DESTROY and BEAT), a filter and an FX sequencer.

firmwares.name: Piterfly
firmwares.author: Piotr Woźniak
firmwares.about: A four-track groovebox for M-VAVE FM-1: 12 synth engines, drums, 24 stored patterns, 128 song positions, 64-step tracks, live granular effects and MIDI THRU. Includes a browser editor with audio preview.

firmwares.name: FM1 Wheel
firmwares.author: ograndebe
firmwares.about: fm1-wheel: a tonewheel organ firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, after setBfree (OpenCode + DeepSeek V4.1 Flash).

firmwares.name: OG Synth
firmwares.author: mikejohnsonbeats
firmwares.about: OG Synth (FM-1 firmware): source of the MPL-2.0 part. Site, installer, manual: https://ogsynth.cc

firmwares.name: saadet
firmwares.author: keremimo
firmwares.about: Single-part synthesizer firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, with Bluetooth MIDI and native 24-bit audio

firmwares.name: Patchwerk
firmwares.author: Matt Kuebrich
firmwares.about: A modular synth for the FM-1. With over 80 modules, including synth engines, samplers, filters, effects, sequencers, and generative tools, you can build, patch, and perform directly on the hardware.

firmwares.name: Sardine
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: Live club mixing for the FM-1: four layers (lead, chord, bass, drums) that play by themselves in 20 styles while you ride them live. Blend one style into the next, build with intros and break-build-drop arcs, edit steps or play a layer by hand. All synthesised, no samples.

firmwares.name: Amenity
firmwares.author: Presethead
firmwares.about: A live jungle tool built around classic breaks (Amen, Apache, Think) and your own. Hold white keys for rolls, builds, echo and Akai-style metallic stretch, play hits on the black keys, and shape the break with variation, warp, ringing feedback, lo-fi, EQ, saturation and compression.

firmwares.name: Flyfish
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: One piece on the FM-1: Chopin's Etude in C major, Op. 10 No. 1, on a sampled Steinway D. Flyfish plays it and lets you shape it, practise it and move it.

firmwares.name: Daurade
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: Grooves in chrome: filtered, pumping, robotic. Press PLAY and Daurade plays a filtered loop that opens over sixteen bars, a mix that pumps on every kick, a robot voice singing the hook and crisp drums. Ten styles; steer it with four knobs, drop it, set off a solo or play the lead yourself.

firmwares.name: LSDJ Burrito
firmwares.author: Dreamy_bacon
firmwares.about: Little Sound Dj, the Game Boy tracker, on the FM-1: played from its keys and knobs, with per-channel filters, drive, lo-fi and an LFO, a shared echo, reverb and compressor, MIDI sync and colour themes. Bring your own LSDj: the project's web page adds it to this firmware on your computer.

firmwares.name: SIDOU
firmwares.author: Denis Sablić
firmwares.about: Turns the FM-1 into a C64 SID machine: two SIDs measured on real chips, a GoatTracker 2 tracker and step sequencer with slide and accent, .sid playback with live tweaks, LAB for sounds with step tables and LFOs, patches from an AI chat or SidStation banks, Bluetooth MIDI, and Live Link in a browser.

firmwares.name: ATEK303
firmwares.author: Animatek
firmwares.about: A TB-303 style acid synth with its own pattern generator: press PLAY and a line plays. Generate, mutate and undo patterns up to 64 steps, edit steps in a piano roll, add drive, chorus, synced delay and plate reverb. The ATEK303 engine from VCV Rack with 14 oscillators and its fine tuning, 12…

firmwares.name: fm1-ripple
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: Ripple: droplets (Lua) and currents (Faust or C) for the M-VAVE FM-1, added over a USB drive without reflashing

firmwares.name: FM1-TRAX
firmwares.author: jartificer
firmwares.about: A Mega Drive / Genesis music tracker. It emulates the YM2612 and SN76489 chips: six FM channels, three square waves and noise, with Deflemask-style effects, 128 FM presets, a drum kit on the DAC, 256 song slots, a demo song and VGM export.

firmwares.name: FM1-GM
firmwares.author: jartificer
firmwares.about: A General MIDI sequencer with 16 tracks, 128 General MIDI instruments to choose from and a drum kit (on track 10). It can store up to 64 songs, each containing up to 128 measures.

firmwares.name: PurpleMonkey
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.about: A first instrument for toddlers: random key bashing and knob turning are rewarded with dancing animated pets and little musical sequences. Press a key, any key.

firmwares.name: FIZZ
firmwares.author: Quixotic7
firmwares.about: A groovebox around one engine, ChoralRoot's FM TONE: eight tracks, p-locks and preset sound locks, conditions, ratchets, chords, and MIDI FX for generative patterns and for reworking the ones you have. Bluetooth MIDI, and recording over USB audio.

firmwares.name: Rainbow Mode
firmwares.author: joshbartlettband-web
firmwares.about: A music toy for little children: 63 cartoon friends, every key in tune, chords, strumming, songs to follow and an ear game, notes on a staff, a volume cap for small ears.

firmwares.name: CHOPPAH
firmwares.author: Laurens Profittlich
firmwares.about: An Amen break chopper for the FM-1: eight classic breaks cut into 16 slices on the white keys, hold a key to loop it. Black keys are momentary pads for rolls, reverse, freeze, tape stop, gate, filter and dub throws. A generator rearranges the break live, with a four-slot FX chain and a DJ filter.

firmwares.name: MIDIMON
firmwares.author: ignis32
firmwares.about: A MIDI monitor for USB, the TRS jack and Bluetooth (as device and host at once): hex or words, filters, stats. Its THRU routes, each filtered, make the FM-1 a Bluetooth MIDI dongle.

firmwares.name: OPLBend Tracker
firmwares.author: AudrenThibault
firmwares.about: LSDJ-style tracker for the M-VAVE FM-1, with an OPL3-style FM engine (not cycle-accurate), circuit bending FX, looper and drum machine. Plays .A2M songs that plays on a real OPL3 with some trackers like AT2 or DOSTRACKER..

firmwares.name: PERF-1
firmwares.author: deamonSLINKY
firmwares.about: A groovebox that plays itself while you steer it: nineteen genres, FM pad, bass, acid and pluck voices, drums with a step sequencer, an auto-DJ, effects you play on the keys, scenes, and a Jam page to play along. Store your pieces, and share them through the online library.

firmwares.name: MOPE-1
firmwares.author: slothpallas
firmwares.about: A sad wavetable synth played by a pixel blob in a rainy room: its eyes are the filter, its mouth the envelope, its tears the delay. Gloomy beats with auto-bass, an arpeggiator, a pattern sequencer, twelve punch effects on the black keys, and presets of your own.

firmwares.name: S1Vave
firmwares.author: Andrew GG
firmwares.about: An 8-voice virtual analog tweak synth: authentic 4-pole resonant filter, dual sub-oscillator, ADSR envelopes, 64-step sequencer, and hands-on live performance controls.

firmwares.name: VIBE FM Link
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: Play the VIBE FM VST plugin with your FM-1. Install this and the FM-1 is the controller: the keys play, KNOB 1-4 and every button do in the plugin what they do on the FM-1 – SLOOP, Felucca, OberVave and the other converted firmwares feel like home, in your DAW, in the Web Player and on the VIBE FM. The sound comes from the plugin, not the FM-1. Plain MIDI: any synth or DAW can learn it too.

firmwares.name: COQUÍ
firmwares.author: saulofilho
firmwares.about: Latin and Caribbean groovebox: synthesized congas, bongos, timbales, guiro and cowbell, 14 grooves from salsa and bomba to dembow, tumbao and montuno lines over the chord you hold, generative parts in the clave, and effect scenes from a backyard to a dub.

firmwares.name: fm1-dock
firmwares.author: Joakim Eriksson
firmwares.about: One firmware, many synths: hold HOME and pick CS-1, Scintilla (the Elka Synthex), OberVave or a sine, no reflashing. Add PROPHET, B3 ORGAN, Niagara Drift, ARTIHIVE, FM-106, FM-1 SID, AMB-1, FoMni, MONK-1, FiMba-1, GATOR or DUB-1 from the page with one click, and your own modules over USB. A master…

firmwares.name: fm1-radio
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: FM-1 internet radio: WiFi, Radio Garden, punch-in FX (source only)

firmwares.name: Dinghy
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: Your base for your own FM-1 or SMK-37 firmware: everything under it done and documented (updates, USB rescue, MIDI over USB and the TRS jack with clock, USB audio, keys, screen, flash storage, an update screen), a 4-voice sine on top, tests and a CI that releases with attestation. Fork it, replace the sine.

firmwares.name: Rhythmer
firmwares.author: Jazzy Rhythmer
firmwares.about: A hands-on groovebox firmware for the FM-1. Shape sounds, build patterns, and find your own groove. Up to six assignable tracks, sound design, sequencing and performance. Free and open source, built on JIANT and reworked by Jazzy Rhythmer.

firmwares.name: ESTAMPIE
firmwares.author: Drew Robinson
firmwares.about: A groovebox for lively mediæval dance music: hurdy-gurdy, lutes, shawms and frame drums over drones, four tracks with 64-step sequencers, mediæval modes and temperaments, and velocity from the FM-1's own keys. Built on GHOULBOX and Felucca.

firmwares.name: Tessera
firmwares.author: Theo Dainis (Rastapopolix)
firmwares.about: Composing through systems on the FM-1. Thirteen generators, or your own steps, make parts that follow, answer and share one harmony. Sections, entries and a shape for the whole piece let a project unfold over minutes or hours. Play it by hand, or let it play.

firmwares.name: SiDJ
firmwares.author: thomasj (tubesockor)
firmwares.about: Plays C64 SID music from HVSC on an emulated 6581 or 8580 and lets you remix every voice live: transpose, mute, solo, swap waveforms, bend envelopes and filter, add LFOs, ride the tempo. Out of the jack, as USB audio or over ASID to a real SID. MIDI clock from the tune, or the tune synced to yours.

firmwares.name: ARTIHIVE
firmwares.author: KHAV
firmwares.about: Eight-voice experimental drone and polyphonic FM synthesizer with four interacting pairs, a 27-key keyboard, envelopes, legato glide, Hyper LFO, stereo motion, dual modulated delay, mutation, DISORDER and a 16-step arpeggiator. Artistically inspired by SOMA LYRA-8; independently developed.

firmwares.name: FM-106
firmwares.author: PatttF
firmwares.about: The Juno-106 emulation of KR-106 ported to the FM-1: six voices on both cores, the BBD stereo chorus, 128 factory presets and a 1980s Roland look.

firmwares.name: HYP-1
firmwares.author: RedtailWorks
firmwares.about: Hypnotic techno and acid: a breathing pad, a deep drone, a generative 303 line and grain over drums you sequence. Flip patterns on the bar, break it down, build it up. Forked from AMB-1. One of a pack of four: LOF-1 (a lofi groovebox), ECO-1 (a plant plays it) and GRAV-1 (a star and its planets), experimental, on its project page.

firmwares.name: LOOM-8
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: A groovebox inspired by the OP-XY: eight tracks on nine engines, step tricks and locks, weave, a conductor and throws.

firmwares.name: CTL-1
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: A MIDI controller: notes in any scale with its chords on the black keys, four banks of knobs, an arpeggiator and Euclidean drums, with General MIDI sounds of its own when nothing is connected.

firmwares.name: ECHOFIELD
firmwares.author: PhilipsKnobs
firmwares.about: A granular sampler: a few seconds of any sound become slow clouds, sparkles, tape loops and swells, played from the keys and knobs. 14 factory sounds, your own samples (or recorded over USB), filter, delay, reverb and tape, and a companion web app for samples, presets and recording.

firmwares.name: Skiff Atlatl
firmwares.author: LIkst4
firmwares.about: Skiff's groovebox with more engines: wavetable, additive, a Moog-style oscillator and a Plaits port, analog-modelled filters, Devilfish-style controls, a step arpeggiator, eight tracks of USB audio to the DAW and screen mirroring.

firmwares.name: AURORA
firmwares.author: twochannels
firmwares.about: Epic cinematic pad, swarm and air synthesis for the FM-1, with generative movement, stereo space, granular freeze and expressive MIDI control.

firmwares.name: Polly
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: A pocket arranger after the QY70: pick a style, play three keys for a chord and a band of eight follows, songs from sections, General MIDI sounds from Sonivox EAS, and a General MIDI module over MIDI in.

firmwares.name: AMB-1
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: A generative ambient machine after Music for Airports: it plays itself from the start, breathing voices, bells on tape loops of unequal length, a gliding bass. You do not perform it, you tend it.

firmwares.name: DX747
firmwares.author: Esben von Buchwald
firmwares.about: An eight-part multitimbral DX7 module. Every part has its own MIDI channel and up to eight layered DX7 voices, with key splits, velocity windows and 64 scenes. A master filter, shared reverb and delay, DX7 ROM import and a web configurator. Played and controlled over MIDI.

firmwares.name: CULTBOX
firmwares.author: beatcult
firmwares.about: A three-channel groovebox: a Polivoks-style duophonic synth (PLVKS), an Elka-style sample drum machine with a step sequencer, and a dub siren, with BBD echoes, per-channel character effects, arp, scales and a mixer with panning.

firmwares.name: Ombak
firmwares.author: Lunar Eclipse Forge
firmwares.about: A gamelan-inspired ensemble. Lead the core melody on the white keys and the ensemble answers: interlocking kotekan, reyong, kendang and gongs in measured Balinese and Javanese tunings, every note shimmering with ombak. Play the traditional forms, or slow it right down for meditation.

firmwares.name: MONK-1
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: Twelve singers, from Jerry the monk to Snider the punk, each in its own voice: MonkSynth's formant voices, played with velocity and pressure from the FM-1's own keys.

firmwares.name: FoMni
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: A chord harp inspired by the Omnichord: strum the white keys, pick chords on the black ones.

firmwares.name: X0X
firmwares.author: Charles Vestal
firmwares.about: A groovebox: 909 and 808 drums, two 303s with TB-3PO, a breakbeat generator and song mode.

firmwares.name: Nauclerus
firmwares.author: Mr. Roboto
firmwares.about: Hortator's eight-track groovebox taken further: ORB Remix with 256 pattern mappings, the TB-3PO acid melody generator with 22 scales, more acid waveshaping, four bipolar LFOs and Grids rhythms copied into editable steps.

firmwares.name: Makohai
firmwares.author: delirioux
firmwares.about: A generative groovebox in the style of early-90s PC tracker music. Six lanes (lead, arp, pad, bass, drums and sfx) play parts composed live in eighteen styles. You don't program steps, you mix styles: blend the next one in lane by lane, shape each lane with tracker effects and call the drop.

firmwares.name: SPAMPY
firmwares.author: Spampy-Droid
firmwares.about: SPAMPY 1.0: a five-track synthwave FM-1 firmware with 170 synth presets, 44 drum kits including KAVINSKY, scenes, effects, new NEON arpeggiator and Slicer modes, extended envelope controls for non-digital engines, and 5 built-in arcade games.

firmwares.name: JAN3000
firmwares.author: JanSchulten
firmwares.about: Community FM-1 firmware (added from our archive).

firmwares.name: boopbox
firmwares.author: Josh-McFarlin
firmwares.about: A live groovebox firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1

firmwares.name: Mighty Arp
firmwares.author: NickCulbertson
firmwares.about: Mighty Arp is custom firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1: a 4-op FM and subtractive hybrid synth built around a chance arpeggiator.

firmwares.name: MIKU-FM1
firmwares.author: MichaelAPerry
firmwares.about: A singing songwriter firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1: a pixel singer sings your songs in Japanese, writes her own, and dances. Free, GPL-3.0; the singer is Hatsune Miku fan art (PCL).

firmwares.name: miaou
firmwares.author: pjac1810
firmwares.about: MIAOU: a kitty keyboard (Meowsic style) for the M-VAVE FM-1, with arpeggiator and 6-track sequencer

firmwares.name: ORBIT
firmwares.author: dspaudio
firmwares.about: A four-track groovebox: three synths and a drum machine in a colour-coded Synth, Drum, Event Tape and Mixer workflow, loops turned into songs, user macros, screens after the OP-1. Based on SLOOP.

firmwares.name: Maestro
firmwares.author: node56
firmwares.about: Maestro: Duolingo-style music lessons on the M-VAVE FM-1. No phone needed.

firmwares.name: Felucca
firmwares.author: Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments)
firmwares.about: The custom firmware the others build on: the FM-1's own synth engines, a sequencer, effects and a better panel, with an editor in the browser.

firmwares.name: Dungeon Tracker
firmwares.author: Bourbon Weather
firmwares.about: Four Track Groovebox with a dungeon crawler cooked into the home screen for the visualizer. Create your party from 8 heroes, store up to 6 sequences then string them together in Song mode!

firmwares.name: SLOOP
firmwares.author: isod89
firmwares.about: A live groovebox: tracks, layers, a step sequencer, song mode, punch-in effects and samples, played on the FM-1 in real time.

firmwares.name: Clipper
firmwares.author: isod89
firmwares.about: A deep synth grown out of SLOOP: 23 engines and 407 sounds, from HYBRID (three oscillators, two filters, a mod matrix) to six-operator FM, wavetables, wave sequencing, a Juno and physical models; arp, step sequencer, MPE and a web editor for every parameter.

firmwares.name: fm1-gio
firmwares.author: GuinanNo1
firmwares.about: GIO-1, A generative electronic disco firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1

firmwares.name: 386DX
firmwares.author: seajaysec
firmwares.about: A karaoke robot with a band: it sings songs from karaoke and MIDI files, or lines you type, to the notes you play. Its face is the voice. Keys, bass and drums play along, with a step sequencer and sixteen punch-in effects.

firmwares.name: Emerald-YM
firmwares.author: CaspiusLabs
firmwares.about: Generative 16-bit music firmware for M-VAVE FM-1: YM2612 FM, Sega-style PSG, live keys and per-instrument effects.

firmwares.name: CLATTER Pocket
firmwares.author: allmyfriendsaresynths
firmwares.about: A generative drum machine on the LXR sound engine. Seven voices, kits grown from a seed in 16 characters, a 64-step sequencer with conditions and per-step pitch, patterns generated and mutated in 11 styles, MIDI notes and clock in, and nine named projects.

firmwares.name: Hortator
firmwares.author: DEADACTIVE
firmwares.about: A drum machine: eight tracks of drums, a step sequencer, Grids, a pumping compressor, LFOs, resonators and live effects. Play it in the browser first.

firmwares.name: Hortator (Bluetooth)
firmwares.author: DEADACTIVE
firmwares.about: Hortator's Bluetooth build: the same eight-track drum machine, plus Bluetooth MIDI for a BLE keyboard or clock, or the M-VAVE SMC-Mixer as a mixer for the eight tracks. Reads the plain version's projects.

firmwares.name: Blop
firmwares.author: Obsimo
firmwares.about: Explore sound with your Blop: one-finger chords from 38 grids, chord rhythms, a bass with its own riffs and a few discreet drums with sidechain, while a little creature swims to your chords in an aquarium on the screen. Chords and bass go out as MIDI over USB.

firmwares.name: SynthMaven
firmwares.author: KingXeryus
firmwares.about: An FM-1 firmware for oriental live musicians, turning the standard M-VAVE FM-1 into an oriental groove box.

firmwares.name: fm1-yoga
firmwares.author: michamilz
firmwares.about: Firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1: sounds for the final relaxation of a yoga class. Guided programs on 174, 396, 432 and 528 Hz from theta to delta (isochronic or binaural), breath, singing bowls and an ambient garden. Handpan, kalimba, bowls and Koshi chimes on the keys. German, English, Sanskrit. Built on fm1-base and AMB-1, MPL-2.0.

firmwares.name: GR!MM
firmwares.author: GR!MM
firmwares.about: Dark ambient, dungeon synth and deathdream firmware: 4 tracks, 7 sound sources, real recorded choirs, tracks that play by themselves, and long tape, granular and reverb effects.

firmwares.name: Vector37
firmwares.author: genkigenki
firmwares.about: An orbiting overtone synth: four corners of two overtone generators each, a sun on a path and a moon around it decide how much of each you hear; the knobs shape the selected planet. Made for the SMK-37, here its FM-1 build. After the Beetlecrab Vector.

firmwares.name: sloopDX
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: SLOOP's live workflow with Dexed's DX7 engine and 128 steps a track: six operators, 32 algorithms, your own .syx banks, every voice edited on the FM-1, FM drums you program.

firmwares.name: sqrl-1
firmwares.author: hed0rah
firmwares.about: SQRL-1 Firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1

firmwares.name: No Man Sky FM
firmwares.author: Hericdk
firmwares.about: A space adventure while you make music, built on SLOOP 2.7.1: fly between planets with two knobs, land, mine, fight sentinels and warp between stars, every SLOOP screen floating over the game.

firmwares.name: analogBEAST
firmwares.author: dzwerg
firmwares.about: M-VAVE FM-1 synth firmware: two DSP routings, Steiner-Parker filter, 128 patterns, SONG and ALBUM modes.

firmwares.name: Melodee
firmwares.author: keremimo
firmwares.about: Total playing pleasure, far beyond Felucca: recording without quantize, microtonal scales, a Casio CZ-1, a bit-by-bit Dexed, scale modes made for an MPC Sample as its companion.

firmwares.name: quadro-fm1
firmwares.author: matttallison
firmwares.about: Arp Quatdra Synthesizer Firmware for the M-Vave FM1

firmwares.name: LUXR
firmwares.author: HOLODECK AUDIOTOOLS
firmwares.about: An LXR-style drum machine: eight sounds, each a synth and a sample layer, with drive, delay, reverb, filter, compressor and limiter. 16 patterns of up to 64 steps, per-track speed, locks, conditional trigs, chains and song mode, MIDI clock and CC learn. Its samples are the Sonic Potions LXR's, non-commercial licence.

firmwares.name: FM1 Quest
firmwares.author: Hericdk
firmwares.about: A pixel-art RPG while you make music, built on SLOOP: four heroes, one a track, walk through a village and fight monsters and bosses as your loop plays, every SLOOP screen redrawn in the game's style.

firmwares.name: DRIFT
firmwares.author: FBNFRTG
firmwares.about: An ambient instrument for live sessions: warm synths, spacious pads and delicate plucks over a generative Euclidean sequencer on one track, with delays and reverbs from spring to shimmer. Built on Felucca.

firmwares.name: Quasar
firmwares.author: nzimas
firmwares.about: Quasar: a firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1 for experimental IDM, after the SOMA Pulsar-23, with an audio engine written from scratch.

firmwares.name: Wanderer
firmwares.author: Nicholas James / Low Vision Music
firmwares.about: Wanderer 1.4: author-tested synth for low-vision musicians. Protect an Anchor, evolve two layers, play 100 sounds, eight Scatter modes and a 13-pattern arp. Adaptive/steady Zoom, clear knob controls, adjustable display hold and optional audio cues.

firmwares.name: B1
firmwares.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
firmwares.about: B1 turns the M-VAVE FM1 into a compact drawbar rock organ with 91 shared tonewheels, nine drawbars per registration, percussion, Leslie, B3/ROCK tones, MIDI and expressive live controls.

firmwares.name: moondaw-fm1
firmwares.author: jaeggerr
firmwares.about: A tracker built for live writing — firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1

firmwares.name: lax32
firmwares.author: pjac1810
firmwares.about: LAX-32: module de sons multitimbral LA (style MT-32)pour M-VAVE FM-1

firmwares.name: grana-fm1
firmwares.author: mongio
firmwares.about: Granulatore di campioni per M-VAVE FM-1 / Granular sample player firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1

firmwares.name: OberVave
firmwares.author: zvenson
firmwares.about: An 8-voice analog-style poly in the spirit of the classic American polys of 1979-84, now on four tracks: each its own sound, arp and sequence; a mixer with chorus, delay, plate reverb and drive sends, a master with DJ filter and compressor. Tracks start on the bar, patterns keep their sounds.

firmwares.name: Niagara Drift
firmwares.author: Evan Yerburgh
firmwares.about: A drone synth inspired by the SOMA Lyra-8, Moog Subharmonicon and Stylophone CPM DS-2. Two virtual-analog drones that breathe and drift on their own, with presets for instant ambient textures and full controls to push them into harsh, beating, self-oscillating sound.

firmwares.name: Kitten Synths
firmwares.author: Black Kitten Devices
firmwares.about: NEW: two drum tracks. Four synths (one a Minimoog-style MUUG with 100 sounds, plus a light LITE synth) and two drum kits play at once, and the FM-1 records 8 channels into your DAW over USB: the stereo master plus each of the six tracks. A SLOOP 2.8 groovebox with the fixes of 2.8.4, 64 steps…

firmwares.name: fm1-x0x-acultur8
firmwares.author: keyboy250
firmwares.about: Acultur8 X0X Extended Edition for M-VAVE FM-1: experimental firmware 0.1.5-beta1, matching source, searchable illustrated FAQ and browser lab.

firmwares.name: Formalfred
firmwares.author: mpancia
firmwares.about: Generative music firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, written in Lean 4 with 313 theorems about it

firmwares.name: Arcturus S6
firmwares.author: Zeptosecond DSP
firmwares.about: An experimental, self-playing wavetable instrument for generative, evolving soundscapes. Four PPG-style oscillators, Serge-style function generators, sample-and-holds and logic, patched through mod and gate matrices. 12 bit, 22kHz, green phosphor CRT, Fairlight-style pages.

firmwares.name: fm-1-impressionism
firmwares.author: darrenjaworski
firmwares.about: mvave-fm1 impressionism firmware

firmwares.name: keySTEP-ONE
firmwares.author: dzwerg
firmwares.about: keySTEP ONE - M-VAVE FM-1 four-track arranger, LIVE PLAY and USB/BLE MIDI (community beta)

firmwares.name: bass-something-2
firmwares.author: imijes
firmwares.about: A monosynth inspired by the legendary Novation Bass Station II, built for the M-VAVE FM-1. Also a companion for Cyma Forma's RND Synth (seeds, locks and a track mixer), and runs on an iPhone or iPad in RemoteFM1.

firmwares.name: NACHTFAHRT
firmwares.author: Cranky Man
firmwares.about: Generative 1970s Berlin School: two sequencers drift against each other over a drone, in eight endless pieces. Play a melody on the white keys and the lead answers it, takes it as its theme and grows new ideas from it.

firmwares.name: theory1
firmwares.author: wave00066
firmwares.about: Music theory firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1: lessons, quizzes and a chord lab (scales, modes, chords, harmony, keys) in English, Italian, Spanish and German.

firmwares.name: Red Mass Vampire OS
firmwares.author: karlalex732-dotcom
firmwares.about: RED MASS VAMPIRE OS FOR M-VAVE FM1 with a lot of new features

firmwares.name: tidepool-fm1
firmwares.author: pjh-133
firmwares.about: Tidepool for the M-VAVE FM-1: an ambient loop instrument as custom firmware. Twelve synthesised scenes, autoplay, and a Blank Canvas to record your own loops.

firmwares.name: Del Rio
firmwares.author: Jess Del Rio
firmwares.about: A rhythm box of ceremony percussion: djembe, cajon, udu, clapsticks, maracas and triangle, their real strokes on the black keys, a step sequencer on the white keys and 31 rhythms from the literature. Played alone: a berimbau with its caxixi, a buzzing tanpura and a breathing shruti box. Built on fm1-base.

firmwares.name: typhoon_fm1
firmwares.author: ignis32
firmwares.about: EWI dedicated FM1 firmware

firmwares.name: OpenIFW
firmwares.author: rcell233
firmwares.about: Community FM-1 firmware (added from our archive).

firmwares.name: fm1-nc-companion
firmwares.author: fenderberg
firmwares.about: NCC 0.4: FM-1 companion for Novation Circuit Tracks. 12 engines, 161 sounds, Circuit macro control, Dual parts and chord drones. Felucca fork.

firmwares.name: Scintilla
firmwares.author: Joakim Eriksson
firmwares.about: The 1981 Elka Synthex on the FM-1: all 80 factory sounds, Paul Wiffen's laser harp among them, checked sample by sample against the original. Two layers of 8 voices (single, split, double), poly, mono or unison, chorus and reverb, and the four knobs edit what is on the screen.

firmwares.name: numetal-skratchmaster-pro-fm1
firmwares.author: mhellar
firmwares.about: NU//METAL SKRATCHMASTER PRO: robot turntablist + nu metal band firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1. Tempo-synced LFO, 17 scratch techniques, mixer. Web MIDI installer. GPL-3, built on Dinghy/Felucca.

firmwares.name: DUB-1
firmwares.author: sbegueria
firmwares.about: A generative dub techno machine that plays itself from the moment it is on: chord stabs into a tape echo, FM pings, a sub bass on five grooves, a ducking kick, crackle, and an eight-bar arrangement with breaks and fills.

firmwares.name: cyma-1
firmwares.author: TEG-Lizard-Man
firmwares.about: CYMA-1 by Team EG & Lizard_Man

firmwares.name: synthesthetic
firmwares.author: michaeljsmalley
firmwares.about: Turns the M-VAVE FM-1 and SMK-37 into an audio/video synth. It's the first firmware for them that sends video over USB, so the instrument shows up as a camera in OBS, Zoom and FaceTime.

firmwares.name: XMOD
firmwares.author: Kot Morderca
firmwares.about: A MOD / XM tracker, sampler and groovebox: play, write and save FastTracker 2 and ProTracker songs on the FM-1, up to 32 channels, with a ProTracker mode for MODs and a song manager in the browser for moving songs to and from the computer.

firmwares.name: ETCH
firmwares.author: Joppe Sikken (SikkenWorks)
firmwares.about: Draw your own waveforms, morph between sounds, and bring them to life with modulation, evolving textures, and powerful effects. From warm analog-inspired tones to wild experimental soundscapes, ETCH puts sound design right at your fingertips.

firmwares.name: FMLarynx
firmwares.author: ejtb76
firmwares.about: A throaty talking formant synth with a 303-style pattern sequencer: The synth is a saw wave through a three-formant vowel filter with an envelope, an added resonant LPF with cutoff and a ping-pong delay with drive. The 16-step sequencer has vowels, accent and slide per step, a pattern randomizer and storage for 16 patterns.

firmwares.name: J6
firmwares.author: JackieAlacrity2373
firmwares.about: A six-voice JUNO-60 style polysynth with chorus, arpeggiator and a 16-step recorder. 56 factory sounds, a MIDI control for every knob, and a free browser editor that plays it over USB-MIDI.

firmwares.name: CINCO
firmwares.author: mrjoshida
firmwares.about: Cinco Identity Generator 2.5 (Celery Man) custom firmware for M-VAVE FM-1

firmwares.name: Felucca-opx
firmwares.author: thomasgregorymarsden-code
firmwares.about: Custom firmware for M-VAVE FM-1: fork of felucca to add a Korg Opsix style engine

firmwares.name: Norilsk
firmwares.author: nzimas
firmwares.about: Norilsk: a firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1 for ambient hellscapes, barren and grim atmospheres and noise -- everything drawn at random, wired at random, torn apart at will.

firmwares.name: Jam Playground
firmwares.author: Bob Perry
firmwares.about: Jam Playground plays a new song the moment you turn the FM-1 on. Four synths and eleven drums sound together. Turn a knob to change the vibe, the scale, a sound, or an effect, and play along.

firmwares.name: Carnac OS
firmwares.author: OrbVorgis
firmwares.about: CARNAC OS is a dual-timbral wavetable synth inspired by neolithic monuments and forgotten rituals. Built for deep sound design and immediate control, with a MAQ 16/3-style sequencer and a J6-style chord arp. The PCM waves need a separate installer: get it from my GitHub page.

firmwares.name: Prysm
firmwares.author: NicholasPratt
firmwares.about: Synth-module firmware for the M-VAVE FM-1, built on Dinghy / Felucca (GPL-3.0)

firmwares.name: Demake
firmwares.author: Sequencist
firmwares.about: An ambient lofi machine on 64 of its author's own pedal recordings: three synths, each with a piano roll, eight patterns, its own reverb, delay or tape echo and motion; huge shared reverbs, colour and old media over the whole mix; a chord machine and an arpeggiator, sixteen scenes, a song mode.

firmwares.name: dwnlo
firmwares.author: jeffwebb-to
firmwares.about: Drum Machine & Synth Custom Firmware for M-VAVE FM-1

firmwares.name: fm1-boardwalk
firmwares.author: charlesvestal
firmwares.about: Boardwalk: a seaside arcade of music games for the M-VAVE FM-1 (fm1-base firmware)

firmwares.name: OrangeCat
firmwares.author: SeattleUser0
firmwares.about: Custom firmware for M-VAVE FM-1

firmwares.name: PT/FM
firmwares.author: hitosu
firmwares.about: A ProTracker-style pocket studio: DX7 FM, JUNO-106, TB-303, chip, sampler and FUSION instruments side by side, 16 voices on both cores, a loop station, a two-deck DJ mode, punch-in effects and over 500 built-in instruments.

firmwares.name: SPELLBOX
firmwares.author: Philippe Jaccoud
firmwares.about: SPELLBOX turns the FM-1 into a talking spelling toy after the 1978 Speak & Spell: an 8-character fluorescent display, a 10-pole LPC voice at 8 kHz through an 8-bit DAC, and the SPELL, LETTER, SAY IT, SECRET CODE and MYSTERY WORD games over four levels, with the keys as an A-to-Z keyboard. SPEAK…

firmwares.name: FM1 SynthDef
firmwares.author: little-scale
firmwares.about: SuperCollider patches on the M-VAVE FM-1: an embedded SynthDef runtime, two-voice instrument and local patch editor.
